docs.title: h3lib
docs.text:
h3lib is a Python geospatial indexing SDK built on Uber H3 (via h3-py). It adds pluggable storage backends, optional caching, index modes, analytics helpers, and native DB H3 where available.

Documentation https://vickykumar7125.github.io/h3lib/ Source github.com/vickykumar7125/h3lib Releases Releases Requires Python ≥ 3.10

docs.title: Why h3lib?
docs.text: Capability What you get H3 surface Indexing, hierarchy, traversal, measures, GeoJSON Index modes h3_index, cell, directed_edge, vertex Persistence SQLite, DuckDB, Postgres (+ PostGIS/h3-pg), MySQL, MongoDB Cache Redis or in-memory Analytics Point→hex aggregation and k-ring smoothing Queries Disk / polygon / edge / vertex lookups over stored data

docs.title: 60-second start
docs.text:
pip install https://github.com/vickykumar7125/h3lib/releases/download/v0.1.0/h3lib-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl

from h3lib import open_client

with open_client("sqlite") as client:
    cell = client.put((37.7749, -122.4194), {"name": "SF"}, resolution=9)
    print(client.get(cell))
    print(client.query_disk(cell, k=1))

docs.text:
1. Installation — conda, extras, wheel from GitHub Releases
  2. Quickstart — common workflows
  3. Stores — choose SQLite, DuckDB, Postgres, MySQL, or Mongo

Official H3 docs

Geometry and algorithm details live in the H3 documentation. h3lib wraps h3-py and focuses on storage, modes, and app-level workflows.

docs.title: Analytics
docs.text: Dataframe-agnostic helpers (no pandas required).

docs.title: aggregate_points
docs.text:
Bin lat/lng points into H3 cells:

from h3lib import open_client

points = [
    (37.7749, -122.4194),
    (37.7750, -122.4195, 2.0),                 # optional weight as 3rd value
    {"lat": 37.7748, "lng": -122.4193, "w": 3},
]

with open_client("sqlite") as client:
    agg = client.aggregate_points(points, resolution=8, weight_key="w")
    # {cell: {"count": N, "weight": W}, ...}

Missing lat/lng keys raise ValueError with a clear message.

docs.title: smooth_disk
docs.text:
Neighborhood average over each cell’s grid disk (stored-subset: only neighbors present in values):

values = {c: v["weight"] for c, v in agg.items()}
smoothed = client.smooth_disk(values, k=1, value_key="weight", include_center=True)

k must be >= 0.

docs.title: Policy
docs.text:
Situation Result cache=False / enabled=False No cache (None) cache=True + Redis URL/client RedisCache cache=True without Redis InMemoryCache Explicit backend="memory" Memory even if redis_url is set 
from h3lib import create_cache, open_client

# Memory
client = open_client("sqlite", cache=True)

# Redis — prefix must be non-empty
client = open_client(
    "sqlite",
    cache=True,
    redis_url="redis://127.0.0.1:6379/0",
    cache_options={"prefix": "h3lib:"},
)

cache = create_cache(enabled=True, backend="memory")
cache = create_cache(enabled=False, backend="redis")  # → None

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
cache.set("cell", {"x": 1}, ttl=60)
cache.get("cell")
cache.set_many({"a": {"v": 1}, "b": {"v": 2}})
cache.get_many(["a", "b"])
cache.delete("a")
cache.clear()   # Redis: SCAN+DELETE under prefix only
cache.close()   # does not close an injected Redis client

In-memory cache is lock-protected for basic thread safety.

Initial public release.

  • Pluggable stores: SQLite, DuckDB, Postgres (PostGIS + h3-pg), MySQL, MongoDB
  • Optional Redis / in-memory cache
  • Index modes: h3_index, cell, directed_edge, vertex
  • Hierarchy, traversal, measures, analytics helpers
  • Docker Compose integration stack
  • CI on Ubuntu / macOS / Windows × Python 3.10–3.14
  • Docs site: https://vickykumar7125.github.io/h3lib/

docs.title: open_client (recommended)
docs.text:
from h3lib import IndexMode, open_client

client = open_client(
    "sqlite",                 # store backend name
    path=":memory:",          # store-specific kwargs are forwarded
    cache=True,               # enable cache
    redis_url=None,           # if set → Redis, else memory when cache=True
    prefer_db=True,           # use native H3 disk queries when available
    index_mode=IndexMode.H3_INDEX,
    stamp_mode_metadata=True,
    default_resolution=9,
    cache_ttl=None,
)

Unknown keyword arguments raise ConfigurationError.

docs.title: H3Client.from_config
docs.text:
from h3lib import H3Client

client = H3Client.from_config(
    store="duckdb",
    store_options={"path": ":memory:", "enable_h3": True},
    cache_enabled=True,
    redis_url=None,
    cache_backend=None,
    cache_options={},
    default_resolution=9,
    prefer_db=True,
    index_mode="h3_index",
    stamp_mode_metadata=True,
)

docs.title: Explicit wiring
docs.text:
from h3lib import H3Client, create_cache, create_store

store = create_store("sqlite", path="h3.db")
cache = create_cache(enabled=True)  # InMemoryCache
client = H3Client(store=store, cache=cache)

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
client = open_client("sqlite")
try:
    ...
finally:
    client.close()

# or
with open_client("sqlite") as client:
    ...

close() closes the store and cache (owned Redis connections only).

docs.title: put / get / delete
docs.text:
from h3lib import open_client

with open_client("sqlite") as client:
    # From point
    cell = client.put((37.7749, -122.4194), {"name": "SF"}, resolution=9)
    # From cell string
    client.put(cell, {"name": "SF", "n": 1})

    print(client.get(cell))
    assert client.delete(cell) is True
    assert client.get(cell) is None

docs.title: Bulk
docs.text:
client.put_many({
    cell: {"n": 1},
    other: {"n": 2},
})
found = client.get_many([cell, other], strict=False)
# strict=True → raise IndexError_ on invalid / wrong-mode indexes

docs.title: Typed helpers
docs.text:
cell = client.put_cell((37.77, -122.42), {"role": "cell"}, resolution=9)

edge = client.put_directed_edge(
    cell,
    destination=client.grid_disk(cell, 1)[1],
    payload={"role": "edge"},
)

vertex = client.put_vertex(cell=cell, vertex_num=0, payload={"corner": 0})

docs.title: put_topology
docs.text:
Stores a cell plus all related directed edges and vertices in one put_many batch:

topo = client.put_topology((37.77, -122.42), {"place": "SF"}, resolution=9)
# {"cells": [...], "directed_edges": [...], "vertexes": [...]}

docs.title: Metadata stamping
docs.text:
When stamp_mode_metadata=True (default), each put adds:

Key Meaning _h3_index Index string _h3_mode cell / directed_edge / vertex _h3_resolution Resolution _h3_valid Validity flag _h3_lat / _h3_lng When known _h3_origin / _h3_destination For edges

User payload keys starting with _h3_ are overwritten while stamping is on.

client = open_client("sqlite", stamp_mode_metadata=False)

docs.title: Hierarchy
docs.text:
H3 parent/child relationships are logical (index hierarchy), not geometric containment.

from h3lib import open_client

with open_client("sqlite") as client:
    cell = client.latlng_to_cell(37.7749, -122.4194, 9)

    parent = client.cell_to_parent(cell, 7)
    children = client.cell_to_children(parent, 9)
    center = client.cell_to_center_child(parent, 9)

    compacted = client.compact_cells(children)   # same-resolution set
    restored = client.uncompact_cells(compacted, 9)

Also available as module functions:

from h3lib import (
    cell_to_parent,
    cell_to_children,
    cell_to_center_child,
    compact_cells,
    uncompact_cells,
)

Note

compact_cells requires a homogeneous resolution set. Mixing resolutions raises an H3 error.

with open_client("sqlite") as client:

from h3lib import index_from_latlng, latlng_to_cell, cell_to_latlng, IndexMode

cell = latlng_to_cell(37.77, -122.42, 9)
cell = index_from_latlng(37.77, -122.42, 9, mode=IndexMode.CELL)

docs.title: Index modes
docs.text:
Mode Value Accepts H3 Index (default) h3_index Any valid H3 index Cell cell Cells only Directed edge directed_edge Directed edges only Vertex vertex Vertices only 
from h3lib import IndexMode, detect_mode, describe_index, open_client

client = open_client("sqlite", index_mode=IndexMode.H3_INDEX)
cell = client.put_cell((37.77, -122.42), {"n": 1}, resolution=9)
print(detect_mode(cell))          # IndexMode.CELL
print(describe_index(cell))       # IndexInfo: mode, res, latlng, details

docs.title: Directed edges & vertices
docs.text:
cell = client.latlng_to_cell(37.77, -122.42, 9)
edges = client.directed_edges(cell)
verts = client.vertexes(cell)
edge = client.cells_to_edge(cell, client.grid_disk(cell, 1)[1])
origin, dest = client.edge_to_cells(edge)
vertex = client.cell_to_vertex(cell, 0)

docs.title: From lat/lng
docs.text:
from h3lib import IndexMode, index_from_latlng

cell = index_from_latlng(37.77, -122.42, 9, mode=IndexMode.CELL)
vertex = index_from_latlng(37.77, -122.42, 9, mode=IndexMode.VERTEX, vertex_num=0)

# Directed edge REQUIRES neighbor= (destination cell)
neighbor = client.grid_disk(cell, 1)[1]
edge = index_from_latlng(
    37.77, -122.42, 9, mode=IndexMode.DIRECTED_EDGE, neighbor=neighbor
)

Positional footgun

put_directed_edge(origin, destination) is wrong — the second positional argument is payload. Use destination=....

docs.title: Measures & GeoJSON
docs.text:
from h3lib import open_client

with open_client("sqlite") as client:
    cell = client.latlng_to_cell(37.7749, -122.4194, 9)

    area = client.cell_area(cell, unit="km^2")
    avg = client.average_hexagon_area(9, unit="km^2")
    n = client.get_num_cells(0)           # 122 at res 0
    res0 = client.get_res0_cells()
    pents = client.get_pentagons(5)

    geo = client.cells_to_geo([cell])     # GeoJSON-like geometry dict

Edge length helpers:

from h3lib import average_hexagon_edge_length, edge_length

edge = client.directed_edges(cell)[0]
print(edge_length(edge, unit="km"))
print(average_hexagon_edge_length(9, unit="km"))

Supported area units follow h3-py (km^2, m^2, …).

docs.title: query_disk (stored subset)
docs.text:
Returns payloads for stored neighbors in the H3 disk — not empty cells.

hits = client.query_disk(cell, k=1, prefer_db=True)
# {cell: payload, ...}  — only indexes present in store/cache

When prefer_db=True (default) and the store supports native H3 (supports_native_h3), the disk is expanded inside DuckDB / Postgres / SQLite UDFs.

docs.title: query_polygon
docs.text:
ring = [
    (37.78, -122.43),
    (37.78, -122.40),
    (37.76, -122.40),
    (37.76, -122.43),
]
hits = client.query_polygon(ring, resolution=9)

Also accepts GeoJSON-like polygon dicts via polygon_to_cells.

docs.title: Edges / vertices from a cell
docs.text:
edge_hits = client.query_edges_from_cell(cell)
vert_hits = client.query_vertexes_from_cell(cell)

docs.title: Raw SQL (trusted operators only)
docs.text:
# DuckDB
rows = client.store.query_cells_sql("SELECT h3_latlng_to_cell(37.77, -122.42, 9)")

# Postgres / SQLite
rows = client.store.query_sql("SELECT ...", params)

Danger

Do not pass untrusted SQL. Table names for SQL stores are identifier-validated; raw SQL helpers are not.

docs.text:
from h3lib import ExtensionError, create_store

try:
    create_store("duckdb", enable_h3=True, require_h3=True)
except ExtensionError as e:
    print(e)  # actionable install guidance

SQL table names must match ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ or schema.table.

docs.title: Traversal
docs.text:
from h3lib import open_client

with open_client("sqlite") as client:
    cell = client.latlng_to_cell(37.7749, -122.4194, 9)

    disk = client.grid_disk(cell, k=1)              # closed disk (includes origin)
    ring = client.grid_ring(cell, k=1)              # hollow ring (excludes origin when k>0)
    pairs = client.grid_disk_distances(cell, k=2)   # [(cell, distance), ...]

    neighbor = ring[0]
    dist = client.grid_distance(cell, neighbor)
    path = client.grid_path_cells(cell, neighbor)

    i, j = client.cell_to_local_ij(cell, neighbor)
    back = client.local_ij_to_cell(cell, i, j)

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• k for grid_disk_distances / smooth_disk must be >= 0 (negative raises IndexError_).
  • grid_disk / grid_ring delegate to h3-py and reject invalid k the same way.
from h3lib import grid_disk, grid_ring, grid_disk_distances, grid_distance, grid_path_cells
